rows.name: IN_NIX_SHELL

problems.statement: CMake takes `python3` from `PATH`. `rust/run-cargo` requires `TRON_NIX_RUST_TOOLCHAIN` and uses that Rust toolchain. `make deb` and `make deb-host` stop with an error.
problems.code_says: The row gives no condition. CMake tests `DEFINED ENV{IN_NIX_SHELL}`, so a set but empty value counts. `rust/run-cargo` and `GNUmakefile` test for a non-empty value.

problems.statement: The `Tron` cell says `Reads and sets`, and the `Where` cell names only readers.
problems.code_says: `flake.nix` sets `pure` in `cmakeSandboxEnvironment` (the Nix CMake builds) and in 4 flake checks, and its `lefthook` wrapper exports `impure`.

cells.Where: `make` (`GNUmakefile`), `cmake` (`cmake/model_selection.cmake`, `ingest/CMakeLists.txt`) and other files. `flake.nix` sets it in its Nix builds, in its checks and in its wrapper for `lefthook` (the Git hook runner).
cells.What Tron does with it: It marks a run inside the Nix dev shell. When it is set, CMake takes `python3` from `PATH`. When it is not empty, `rust/run-cargo` uses the Rust toolchain of `TRON_NIX_RUST_TOOLCHAIN`, and `make deb` and `make deb-host` stop with an error.

evidence: cmake/model_selection.cmake:45 - `if(DEFINED ENV{IN_NIX_SHELL})` runs `command -v python3` and uses the result as the Python for model definitions
ingest/CMakeLists.txt:216 - `if(DEFINED ENV{IN_NIX_SHELL})` uses that same Python for the export; lines 244 and 275 skip the pinned GHC and cabal version check when it is defined
rust/run-cargo:10 - `[[ -n "${IN_NIX_SHELL:-}" ]]`; line 11 stops when `TRON_NIX_RUST_TOOLCHAIN` is unset or empty; line 34 runs `$TRON_NIX_RUST_TOOLCHAIN/bin/cargo`

GNUmakefile:629 - with goal `deb-host`, line 630 tests for a non-empty value and line 631 is `$(error ...)`

rows.name: LDFLAGS

problems.statement: On Linux, `flake.nix` sets `-lgcc_s` in the Nix dev shells.
problems.code_says: Only the shells from `mkTronDevShell` (`default`, `tools`, `cuda`) and the shell `cmake-sandbox` get it. Shells such as `minimal`, `ingest` and `lint` do not. The Nix builds `tron-cmake-test-build` and `tron-cmake-sandbox-configure` also get it through `cmakeSandboxEnvironment`.

problems.statement: A source comment says that `libgcc_s` gives the unwinding symbols for builds with `--rtlib=compiler-rt`.
problems.code_says: The sentence reports a comment (house rule 6). The code shows only the value `-lgcc_s`. No code in the checkout ties `LDFLAGS` to `--rtlib=compiler-rt`.

cells.Where: `make` in `bin/iotools-1.5`, a copy of iotools (a third-party hardware register tool) (`bin/iotools-1.5/Makefile`). `flake.nix` sets it for the build tools in Nix dev shells and Nix builds.

rows.name: MAKECMDGOALS

problems.statement: Slice then labels its Dice work `make <goals>`.
problems.code_says: `_infer_label_from_env` returns a non-empty `DICE_LABEL` first. It uses `MAKECMDGOALS` only when `DICE_LABEL` is unset or empty after the removal of spaces.
The test script is not a reader. It removes the variable with `unset` and with `env -u` before it starts `make`.

cells.Where: `make` (`GNUmakefile`), `slice` (`bin/slice`). `bin/ci/test-make-environment-guidance.sh` removes it for the `make` commands that it starts.

rows.name: MAKEFLAGS

cells.Where: `make` (`GNUmakefile`). `bin/ci/test-generated-output-staging.sh` sets it for `cmake --build`. `bin/ci/test-make-environment-guidance.sh` removes it for `make` commands that it starts.
cells.What Tron does with it: The makefile appends `--no-print-directory -j $(NPROC_BUILD)`. For a remote build, a `-jN` option in it sets `REMOTE_BUILD_CORES` to N. The option `-B` also reaches the `make` command on the LSF worker.

evidence: GNUmakefile:209 - `MAKEFLAGS += --no-print-directory -j $(NPROC_BUILD)`

bin/bsub-build:15 - `cores=${REMOTE_BUILD_CORES:-16}`
bin/ci/test-generated-output-staging.sh:491 - `MAKEFLAGS=--no-print-directory cmake --build "$@"`

unresolved: LDFLAGS - which link commands of the Tron build inside the Nix dev shell get `-lgcc_s` from this variable. The Linux CMake presets set `CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS`, `CMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS` and `CMAKE_MODULE_LINKER_FLAGS` themselves (CMakePresets.json:25). The CMake documentation says that CMake reads `LDFLAGS` only to give these variables their first value. The row therefore states no effect on the Tron build. The link lines of `ninja -v` in a new build directory inside the Nix dev shell settle it.

GHCRTS - the order in which the GHC runtime applies its options (the built-in `-with-rtsopts` text first, then `GHCRTS`, then the command line) comes from the GHC User's Guide, not from repository code. The guide section on the `GHCRTS` environment variable settles it, or one run of the built `ingest` program with `GHCRTS=-N4 ... +RTS -s`, which prints the thread count in use.

MAKE - whether a `MAKE` value from the environment replaces the value that GNU Make gives the variable itself. The row says only that the recipes run the command in `MAKE`, which holds in both cases. One run of `MAKE=echo make -n format`, or the GNU Make manual on the origin of `MAKE`, settles it. Running make in the checkout was not allowed here.
notes: 12 rows of section 7.3 checked against commit 7eddde7895. No row contradicts the code. Unchanged (3): DESTDIR, EXTRA_CFLAGS, MAKE. Changed for a fact (3): IN_NIX_SHELL, LDFLAGS, MAKECMDGOALS. IN_NIX_SHELL now separates the two tests in the code: CMake tests for a set value (cmake/model_selection.cmake:45) and the scripts and the makefile test for a non-empty value (rust/run-cargo:10, GNUmakefile:573). Its Where cell now names the setter, `flake.nix`. To stay within 40 words, the cell no longer says that `rust/run-cargo` stops without `TRON_NIX_RUST_TOOLCHAIN`. The row of that variable says it. MAKECMDGOALS now says that a non-empty `DICE_LABEL` takes priority for the label (bin/slice:5483), and its Where cell says that the test script removes the variable.
